summary:
Short answer: II_DGE=hw is not safe as originally written. I reproduced the crash deterministically, worked out the conditions that trigger it, and found a variant that is both faster and showed no faults in testing: all DMAs on hw DGE, but both indirect weight DMAs issued from the SP (sync) queue instead of alternating SP/ACT.

1) Reproduction. The original crash comes back exactly with the old blob kernel (ii_fused11a, WSA_FN=0, hw): BAD_OPCODE on the sequencer, MD Info 0xb8, Block Id 2. It only hits the odd physical core of each LNC2 pair (NC1/3/5/7), at the first execution of the batch-8/1024 decode NEFF, inside the first fused-MoE call of layer 0. The even cores then wait, which produces the "hang after ALLREDUCE" messages. "1004" is the NEFF id, not a status code. I got the same crash with the current P2 kernel: config C with WSA_FN=0 and II_DGE=hw dies at the same warmup step.

2) Root cause, as far as I could pin it.
- It depends on what ran before. The exact same NEFF (c803…) runs clean 20 times standalone, and also runs clean when it is the first decode NEFF after prefill. It faults only when the batch-4 decode NEFFs have executed first. A 7-minute minimal repro is decode buckets [4,8] x [1024].
- The faulting PC changes from run to run (0xaae, 0x4ae, 0xcbb) while the stuck instruction pointers stay the same. So the PC is a position in a runtime ring, not an instruction in the NEFF.
- Turning the execution barrier on (NEURON_RT_DISABLE_EXECUTION_BARRIER=0) does not help. NEURON_RT_DBG_DISABLE_DGE_BOUND_CHECK=1 makes it worse (hang already in prefill).
- Runtime debug logs map engine id 2 to GPSIMD (Pool). Instruction streams are fed through per-engine refill rings, and a model-switch preamble is inserted at every NEFF switch.
- Which DMAs matter (blob kernel, crashing history): it crashes only when all DMAs are hw with weight DMAs alternating SP/ACT. Each of these single changes makes it pass: weights hw + static DMAs sw; weights sw + static DMAs hw; no oob-skip (padding redirected); weight DMAs only on the sync queue.
- My reading: this is not a bug in the kernel's logic (accuracy and NaN tests are unaffected). It is a runtime/firmware hazard tied to the ACT engine issuing hw-DGE DMAs, which roughly doubles the ACT instruction stream (5.9k to 13.9k instructions in the batch-8 P2 NEFF), under a particular NEFF-switch history. I could not pin the hardware mechanism further without ISA docs. The repro is worth sending to the Neuron runtime team.

3) Config C with WSA_FN=1 and all-hw (alternating queues) showed no fault: 67-minute mixed soak, 2,678 requests, 0 failures, 13/13 NaN passes, 0 runtime error lines. Warmup alone also passed with three different bucket subsets, including the [4,8]x[1024] history that kills WSA_FN=0. But it is the same hazard class, so I'd treat it as unproven rather than safe.

4) Variants tested:
- Weights hw + static DMAs sw: no faults (68 min with WSA_FN=0, 67 min with WSA_FN=1), but c1 gets slower (6.58 vs 6.44 ms).
- Sync-queue variant (env ND_QGU=sync ND_QDN=sync, everything else hw): with WSA_FN=0 it passes the warmup that crashed and a 68-minute soak with 0 errors. With WSA_FN=1 it ran 71 minutes of soak across two server runs (2,884 requests, 0 failures, 14/14 NaN passes), after the perf runs. Moving the weight DMAs off ACT cuts the ACT stream from 13.9k to 6.2k instructions, and it is the fastest variant.

5) Accuracy (GSM8K 500): sw 0.932 and 0.936 on two runs (6 flips between them); all-hw 0.934; sync-queue 0.922 and 0.932. The two sync-queue runs differ by 7 flips from each other, and run 2 differs from sw by only 2, so the 0.922 looks like run-to-run noise.

6) Cache pitfall you should know about. The NKI compile cache key ignores trace-time env such as II_DGE. With a warm cache, switching to hw silently reuses the old sw kernel. My first "hw" run was actually sw; I caught it by comparing per-engine instruction counts in the NEFFs, and I kept that run as the sw reference. To get a real build you must drop the whole vc/neuron/compile_cache/nki directory. Dropping only the fused-kernel entries breaks compilation (NCC_EVRF059, missing /var/tmp kernel files).

Second pitfall: pkill on "vllm serve" leaves the VLLM::EngineCore and VLLM::Worker processes alive and holding the device, so the next server fails to start. Kill "VLLM::" processes too.
numbers:
TPOT in ms, measured on the same pod and same protocol (prefix-cache reset, warm-up seed 7). Columns: sw (config C) / hw alternating queues / weights-hw + static-sw / hw sync-queue.
- c1 ShareGPT s42: 6.44 / 6.46 / 6.58 / 6.39
- c1 own client: 6.44 / 6.47 / 6.58 / 6.39
- c1 random 256: 6.44 / 6.45 / 6.58 / 6.38
- c1 random 1024: 6.46 / 6.48 / 6.62 / 6.43
- c4 ShareGPT s42: 11.50 / 11.49 / 11.36 / 11.15
- c4 ShareGPT s123: 11.56 / 11.60 / 11.68 / 11.39
- c4 own client: 11.30 / 11.25 / 11.36 / 11.12
- c4 random 6000: 14.78 / 14.32 / 14.42 / 14.16
- c16 ShareGPT s42: 24.11 / 23.49 / 23.60 / 23.56 (throughput 631.8 / 648.9 / 647.4 / 648.4 tok/s)
- c16 ShareGPT s123: 24.06 / 23.70 / 23.71 / 23.71
- c16 own client: 23.36 / 23.09 / 23.14 / 22.96 (throughput 651 / 657 / 658 / 662 tok/s)
- c16 random 7000: 43.84 / 43.43 / 43.33 / 43.54

Gain of sync-queue hw vs sw: c1 about -0.05 ms (-0.8%), c4 -0.17 to -0.35 ms (-1.5 to -3%, -4% at 6000 context), c16 -0.35 to -0.55 ms (-1.5 to -2.3%, +2.6% throughput). Plain hw with alternating queues gives no c1 gain (+0.02 ms), about 0 at c4 short contexts, and -1.2 to -2.6% at c16. TTFT is unchanged; prefill does not use this kernel.

Crash vs pass (warmup, batch-8 after batch-4 history):
- Crash: blob kernel all-hw WSA_FN=0 (4/4 runs, plus 2 more with debug logging or the barrier enabled); P2 all-hw WSA_FN=0.
- Pass: the same NEFF as the first decode graph; weights-hw only; static-DMAs-hw only; no oob-skip; weight DMAs on sync queue; P2 weights-hw + static-sw with WSA_FN=0; P2 sync-queue with WSA_FN=0.

Soaks (mixed ShareGPT c1/c2/c4/c16 plus random 180-7000 input, about 5-minute iterations, NaN test each iteration):
- hw alternating, WSA_FN=1: 67 min, 2,678 requests, 0 failures, 13/13 NaN, 0 errors
- weights-hw + static-sw, WSA_FN=0: 68 min, 2,678 requests, 0 failures, 13/13 NaN
- weights-hw + static-sw, WSA_FN=1: 67 min, 2,678 requests, 0 failures, 13/13 NaN
- sync-queue, WSA_FN=0: 68 min, 2,678 requests, 0 failures, 13/13 NaN
- sync-queue, WSA_FN=1: 31 + 41 min, 2,884 requests, 0 failures, 14/14 NaN
- Warmup with alternate bucket subsets: 5/5 pass

GSM8K 500 accuracy: sw 0.932 / 0.936; hw alternating 0.934; weights-hw + static-sw 0.924 (WSA_FN=0) and 0.932 (WSA_FN=1); sync-queue 0.934 (WSA_FN=0), 0.922 and 0.932 (WSA_FN=1). Flip counts are 2-11 per comparison, the same range as sw against itself (6).

Minimal crash repro: package /tmp/trn2-hyd/ii/pr56 + cache /data/cache/ie_int_fn0 + Q3_FUSED_MOE_KMOD=ii_fused11a II_DGE=hw WSA_FN=0, buckets num_seqs [4,8], decode context [1024] (about 7 min)
integration:
My recommendation is the sync-queue variant, as an opt-in rather than the default.

1. Copy /tmp/trn2-hyd/nd/k/p2d_fused.py into pkg_a, next to p2_fused11n.py. With no ND_* variables set it behaves exactly like p2_fused11n.
2. Run config C with Q3_FUSED_MOE_KMOD=p2d_fused II_DGE=hw ND_QGU=sync ND_QDN=sync. All other env and serve flags stay as in config C.
3. Build the cache with `python3 mkbase.py /data/cache/cb_B <new_cache> ""`, or start from /data/cache/nd_q1, which already has it compiled. Skipping this step silently gives you the sw kernel, because the NKI compile cache ignores II_DGE.
4. Check the build: the batch-8 decode NEFF should have about 6.2k ACT and about 19k SP instructions per core (dget.py). The sw build has a large Pool count instead.

Two things to avoid:
- Never combine WSA_FN=0 with all-hw on alternating queues; it crashes deterministically.
- Don't use weights-hw with static DMAs on sw; it is slower at c1.

If you want zero risk, keep II_DGE=sw. The hw gain is only 1-3%.

Also fix the kill step in any server script: kill the "VLLM::" processes as well as "vllm serve", or the next server cannot get the device.
open_issues:
- The exact hardware/runtime mechanism is not pinned down. Everything points to GPSIMD (Pool) instruction refill or the model-switch path when hw-DGE DMAs are issued from the ACT queue, but I could not get further without ISA docs or Neuron runtime help. The deterministic repro should be filed with the Neuron team. "Every small change avoids it" means the sync-queue variant passing is empirical evidence, not proof. It ran 72 min (WSA_FN=1) and 68 min (WSA_FN=0) with no faults, but a longer canary soak (several hours of production-like traffic) is advisable before making it the default.
- Plain all-hw with alternating queues and WSA_FN=1 also showed no fault, but it is the same hazard class and gives a smaller gain. Leave it off.
- The 7-minute sync-queue soak loop doesn't hit NEFF-switch patterns that never occur in it, e.g. very long runs at one bucket followed by a rare one. A randomized NEFF-switch stress test over every (batch, context) pair would strengthen the evidence.
- Not done: comparing hw for gate_up only against sync-queue. Sync-queue already beats every DMA-class split I measured, and its gain matches what an idle ACT engine would explain.
- Leftover scratch cache /data/cache/nd_swg (about 200 MB, a copy of cb_B) can be deleted. My cleanup command didn't remove it before the pods were deleted. nx-d and nx-d2 are deleted. I did not touch nx-j, nx-j2 or trn2-holder.
